{"documentId": "f_a37b403d5200d4f0a31d31", "title": "Stockholder close-out notes", "name": "Stockholder close-out notes", "revisionId": "3c986c6ce3", "createdTime": "2026-02-13T01:05:41Z", "modifiedTime": "2026-02-13T01:05:41Z", "text": "Stockholder close-out notes

These replace my earlier outreach notes.

What needs doing
- the reach-out I promised to the investors, one by one, not one mail to everyone
- where I left things today in #winddown: the angels are what's open from my list, besides the Sunset onboarding
- the investor email on the Task List: take my draft from #winddown and bring it up to date as a letter I can send. the update outline has the sections
- the holder sheet comes first, the notes and everything else run off it. Share it and the letter with Robert
- notes ready for me by Tuesday, as Gmail drafts. I said I'd archive google after the 15th but that waits, we keep it until the data is extracted, so my drafts are safe until I've gone through them. I read and send each note myself
- everything goes in the close-out folder, not the Wind Down one, that one is the vendor and termination papers
- Griffin's partner gets a heads-up as a reply on the Feb 12 Board position thread, with what we still need from Griffin. That one can go out once the sheet is right
- when the sheet is ready, reply under my list in #winddown and say who goes first

How each holder gets handled
- Carta is the record. If a line's last day has passed, it holds nothing.
- One row per issue on the sheet and at most one note per person. The three of us only go in the totals.
- Told means a written message about the closing, sent to them directly, from one of the three of us; for a fund, its partner.
- Everyone still holding something gets what they are owed: the closing if they have not been told, their last day if they have one. Whoever's last day comes first goes first.
- Each note says what they hold.
- Anything they asked about their holding that we never answered gets answered in their note, if they get one.
- Notice route: the email we have, unless a document says otherwise.

Labels for the sheet: Nothing, Already told, Closing, Last day, Closing and last day.
"}

Despite multiple iterations, we did not get the metrics to a point that supports a viable business path, and we do not have the funding to continue operating while searching for a new direction.
What we did and what we learned
• We built and tested three games on a limited budget, staying true to our mission of hybridcasual gameplay with RPG depth.
• We took real creative risks and pushed to innovate:
Domino Delights: Domino/Tripeak solitaire gameplay with RPG elements
Zombie Match 3D: Match Factory style core loop with RPG combat/progression elements
Combo Fighter: Tetris-like block gameplay with RPG elements
• We also explored partnerships and other paths to scale distribution and improve outcomes, but none changed the trajectory enough.
Financial context
• We have been in sustained financial hardship since mid-2025.
• Revenue did not reach meaningful levels, and the plans we pursued to change that did not work.
• Given our current runway of less than a month and obligations, continuing would create risk without a responsible probability of success.
What happens next
• We are initiating an orderly wind-down process and preparing the required board resolutions and documentation.
• Our priorities are to handle employee and contractor obligations properly, meet tax and compliance requirements, close out vendor commitments, and Sunset the products in a controlled way.
• We will also evaluate what to do with the remaining IP and codebase (archive, sale, or other disposition) and will keep you informed.
Timeline and updates
• We will share a more detailed wind-down plan and timeline shortly, including key dates for operational shutdown.
• I will send periodic updates as we complete the major steps and once we have clarity on final liabilities and any remaining assets.
I regret having to send this. I am proud of the team we put together and the quality of what we shipped. We ran a frugal operation, made multiple bets, and pushed hard, but we did not reach the performance required to build a durable company.

I got your email from my good friend PERSON_2710_NAME at Super Evil Megacorp.
My name is Leonard Hayes and I'm the CEO and co-founder of [SOURCE_ORG_0001].

I’m reaching out because we are shutting down [SOURCE_ORG_0001], Inc. and want
to make sure we execute an orderly wind-down properly.

We are a Delaware corporation, qualified to do business in North Carolina
and California. We have preferred stock from a seed round (no SAFEs). We
have no US employees other than ourselves and only 4 international
contractors. We are out of funds and want to avoid missteps around creditor
ha[USERNAME_11664], state Withdrawals, tax filings, and closing operational accounts
cleanly.

We are looking for help with a managed wind-down, including:

   -

   A practical wind-down plan and timeline
   -

   Vendor termination support
   -

   Creditor communications and claim handling approach
   -

   Delaware dissolution and withdrawals in CA and NC, plus tax/accounting
   closeout coordination
   -

   Guidance on reserves and any final distributions consistent with
   preferred stock terms

If this is in your wheelhouse, can we set up a short call this week? I can
share our current cash position, liabilities list, and key contracts in
advance.

Thank you,
Leonard Hayes

table that we can share with investors.

approach and asked for a pro forma and what the post-transaction cap will
look like.

Goal: make the company investable again at a true pre-seed risk profile,
while treating participating investors fairly and clearly.

hour or on Friday to re-introduce you to my co-founders and to discuss.

Best,
Leonard

Side Letter\\nLadies and Gentlemen:\\nThis letter agreement is to confirm in writing an agreement made by HARMONY GAMES, Inc., a Delaware corporation (the \\u201cCompany\\u201d), with the investor set out above (the \\u201cInvestor\\u201d), in connection with the Investor\\u2019s conditional agreement to invest in the Company on or about the date hereof, based on the Series Seed Preferred Stock Purchase Agreement, Investor\\u2019s Rights Agreement (the \\u201cIRA\\u201d), Right of First Refusal and Co-Sale Agreement and Voting Agreement each by and among the Company, the Investor and the other parties thereto (such agreements, individually and collectively, and each as may be amended and restated from time to time, the \\u201cFinancing Documents\\u201d). Capitalized terms not otherwise defined herein shall have the meaning set forth in the Financing Documents.\\nThe terms of this letter agreement are, notwithstanding the terms of any Financing Documents or the Company\\u2019s certificate of incorporation or bylaws (together, the \\u201cConstitutional Documents\\u201d) or any definitive agreement entered into in connection with the Financing Documents in the Equity Financing (collectively, including the Financing Documents and the Constitutional Documents, for the avoidance of doubt, each as may be amended and restated from time to time, the \\u201cCompany Documents\\u201d) in furtherance and not in limitation of any similar rights or provisions of the Investor set out therein. In the event of a conflict between the terms of this letter agreement, on the one hand, and the terms of any Company Document, on the other hand, the terms of this letter agreement are intended to and shall control.\\nCap Table. Upon request by an Investor, the Company will promptly deliver to the Investor a summary fully diluted capitalization table, with sufficient detail to enable Investor to calculate its ownership interest in the Company on a fully diluted basis.\\nNotices. THIS SERIES SEED PREFERRED STOCK PURCHASE AGREEMENT (this “Agreement”), is made as of [________], 2023, by and among Harmony Games Inc., a Delaware corporation (the “Company”) and the investors listed on Exhibit A attached to this Agreement (each a “Purchaser” and together the “Purchasers”).
The parties hereby agree as follows:
Purchase and Sale of Preferred Stock.
Sale and Issuance of Preferred Stock.  The Company shall have adopted and filed with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware on or before the Initial Closing (as defined below) the Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation in the form of Exhibit B attached to this Agreement (the “Restated Certificate”).  Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, each Purchaser agrees to purchase at the applicable Closing (as defined below) and the Company agrees to sell and issue to each Purchaser at the applicable Closing that number of shares of Series Seed Preferred Stock, $0.0001 par value per share (the “Series Seed Preferred Stock”), set forth opposite each Purchaser’s name on Exhibit A, at a purchase price of $[__] per share.  The shares of Series Seed Preferred Stock issued to the Purchasers pursuant to this Agreement shall be referred to in this Agreement as the “Shares.”
Closing; Delivery.
The initial purchase and sale of the Shares shall take place remotely via the exchange of documents and signatures on the date hereof, or at such other time and place as the Company and the Purchasers mutually agree upon, orally or in writing (which time and place are designated as the “Initial Closing”).  In the event There is more than one closing, the term “Closing” shall apply to each such closing unless otherwise specified.
At each Closing, the Company shall deliver to each Purchaser, upon request, a notice of issuance with respect to the Shares being purchased by such Purchaser at such Closing against payment of the purchase price therefor by check payable to the Company, by wire or other electronic transfer to a bank account designated by the Company, by cancellation or conversion of indebtedness or other convertible securities of the Company to Purchaser, by any method mutually agreeable between the Company and the Purchaser, or by any combination of such methods.
Sale of Additional Shares of Preferred Stock.  After the Initial Closing, the Company may sell, on the same terms and conditions as those contained in this Agreement, up to that number of authorized but unsold shares of Series Seed Preferred Stock (the “Additional Shares”), to one (1) or more purchasers (the “Additional Purchasers”) reasonably acceptable to GRIFFIN GAMING PARTNERS II, L.P., provided that (i) such subsequent sale is consummated prior to ninety (90) days after the Initial Closing and (ii) each Additional Purchaser becomes a party to the Transaction Agreements (as defined below), by executing and delivering a counterpart signature page to each of the Transaction Agreements.  Exhibit A to this Agreement shall be updated to reflect the number of Additional Shares purchased at each such Closing and the parties purchasing such Additional Shares.
Defined Terms Used in this Agreement.  In addition to the terms defined above, the following terms used in this Agreement shall be construed to have the meanings set forth or referenced below.
“Affiliate” means, with respect to any specified Person, any other Person who, directly or indirectly, controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with such Person, including, without limitation, any general partner, managing member, officer, director or trustee of such Person, or any venture capital fund or registered investment company now or hereafter existing that is controlled by one (1) or more general partners, managing members or investment advisers of, or shares the same management company or investment adviser with, such Person.
“Code” means the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended.
“Company Intellectual Property” means all Intellectual Property, licenses in, to and under any Intellectual Property, and in any and all such cases that are owned or purported to be owned or used by the Company in the conduct of the Company’s business as now conducted and as presently proposed to be conducted.
“Indemnification Agreement” means the agreement between the Company and the director designated by any Purchaser entitled to designate a member of the Board of Directors pursuant to the Voting Agreement, dated as of the date of the Initial Closing, in the form of Exhibit D attached to this Agreement.
“Intellectual Property” means all patents, patent applications, registered and unregistered trademarks, trademark applications, registered and unregistered service marks, service mark applications, tradenames, copyrights, trade secrets, domain names, information and proprietary rights and processes, similar or other intellectual property rights, subject matter of any of the foregoing, and tangible embodiments of any of the foregoing.
“Investors’ Rights Agreement” means the agreement among the Company and the Purchasers dated as of the date of the Initial Closing, in the form of Exhibit E attached to this Agreement.
“Key Employee” means any executive-level employee (including division director and vice president-level positions) as well as any employee or consultant who either alone or in concert with others develops, invents, programs or designs any material Company Intellectual Property.
“Knowledge” including the phrase “to the Company’s knowledge” shall mean the actual knowledge of the following persons: [PERSON_NAME_0357], [PERSON_NAME_0174] and Arthur.  Additionally, for purposes of Section 2.8, the Company shall be deemed to have “knowledge” of a patent right if the Company has actual knowledge of the patent right or would be found to be on notice of such patent right as determined by reference to United States patent laws.
“Material Adverse Effect” means a material adverse effect on the business, assets (including intangible assets), liabilities, financial condition, property, prospects or results of operations of the Company.
“Person” means any individual, corporation, partnership, trust, limited liability company, association or other entity.
“Purchaser” means each of the Purchasers who is initially a party to this Agreement and any Additional Purchaser who becomes a party to this Agreement at a subsequent Closing under Section 1.3.
“Right of First Refusal and Co-Sale Agreement” means the agreement among the Company, the Purchasers, and certain other stockholders of the Company, dated as of the date of the Initial Closing, in the form of Exhibit F  attached to this Agreement.
“Securities Act” means the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and the rules and regulations promulgated thereunder.
“Transaction Agreements” means this Agreement, the Investors’ Rights Agreement, the Right of First Refusal and Co-Sale Agreement, and the Voting Agreement.
“Voting Agreement” means the agreement among the Company, the Purchasers and certain other stockholders of the Company, dated as of the date of the Initial Closing, in the form of Exhibit G attached to this Agreement.
Representations and Warranties of the Company.  The Company hereby represents and warrants to each Purchaser that, except as set forth on the Disclosure Schedule attached as Exhibit C to this Agreement, which exceptions shall be deemed to be part of the representations and warranties made hereunder, the following representations are true and correct as of the date of the Initial Closing, except as otherwise indicated.  The Disclosure Schedule shall be arranged in sections corresponding to the numbered and lettered sections contained in this Section 2, and the disclosures in any section of the Disclosure Schedule shall qualify other sections in this Section 2 only to the extent it is readily apparent from a reading of the disclosure that such disclosure is applicable to such other sections.
For purposes of these representations and warranties (other than those in Sections 2.2, 2.3, 2.4, 2.5, and 2.6), the term the “Company” shall include any subsidiaries of the Company, unless otherwise noted herein.
Organization, Good Standing, corporate Power and Qualification.  The Company is a corporation duly organized, validly existing and in good standing under the laws of the State of Delaware and has all requisite corporate power and authority to carry on its business as now conducted and as presently proposed to be conducted.  The Company is duly qualified to transact business and is in good standing in each jurisdiction in which the failure to so qualify would have a Material Adverse Effect.
Capitalization.
The authorized capital of the Company consists, immediately prior to the Initial Closing and following the filing of the Restated Certificate (unless otherwise noted), of:
[__________] shares of common stock, $0.0001 par value per share (the “Common Stock”), [_________] shares of which are issued and outstanding immediately prior to the Initial Closing.  All of the outstanding shares of Common Stock have been duly authorized, are fully paid and nonassessable and were issued in compliance with all applicable federal and state securities laws.
[__________] shares of Preferred Stock,  of which [__________] shares have been designated Series Seed Preferred Stock, none of which are issued and outstanding immediately prior to the Initial Closing.  The rights, privileges and preferences of the Preferred Stock are as stated in the Restated Certificate and as provided by the Delaware General Corporation Law.  Upon the Initial Closing, each outstanding share of Preferred Stock will initially be convertible into one (1) share of Common Stock.
The Company has reserved [__________] shares of Common Stock for issuance to officers, directors, employees and consultants of the Company pursuant to its [2023 Stock Plan] duly adopted by the Board of Directors and approved by the Company stockholders (the “Stock Plan”).  Of such reserved shares of Common Stock, [__________] shares have been issued pursuant to restricted stock purchase agreements, options to purchase [__________] shares have been granted and are currently outstanding, and [__________] shares of Common Stock remain available for issuance to officers, directors, employees and consultants pursuant to the Stock Plan.  The Company has furnished to the Purchasers complete and accurate copies of the Stock Plan and forms of agreements used thereunder.
Section 2.2(c) of the Disclosure Schedule sets forth the capitalization of the Company immediately following the Initial Closing including the number of shares of the following: (i) issued and outstanding Common Stock; (ii) outstanding stock options; (iii) shares of Common Stock reserved for future award grants under the Stock Plan; (iv) each series of Preferred Stock; and (v) warrants or stock purchase rights, if any.  Except for (A) the conversion privileges of the Shares to be issued under this Agreement, (B) the rights provided in Section 4 of the Investors’ Rights Agreement, and (C) the securities and rights described in Sections 2.2(a)(ii) and 2.2(b) of this Agreement and Section 2.2(c) of the Disclosure Schedule, There are no outstanding options, warrants, rights (including conversion or preemptive rights and rights of first refusal or similar rights) or agreements, orally or in writing, to purchase or acquire from the Company any shares of Common Stock or Preferred Stock, or any securities convertible into or exchangeable for shares of Common Stock or Preferred Stock.  All outstanding shares of the Company’s Common Stock and all shares of the Company’s Common Stock underlying outstanding options are subject to (i) a right of first refusal in favor of the Company upon any proposed transfer (other than transfers for estate planning purposes); and (ii) a lock-up or market standoff agreement of not less than one hundred eighty (180) days following the Company’s initial public offering pursuant to a registration statement filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission under the Securities Act.
None of the Company’s stock purchase agreements or stock option documents contains a provision for acceleration of vesting (or lapse of a repurchase right) or other changes in the vesting provisions or other terms of such agreement or understanding upon the occurrence of any event or combination of events, including, without limitation, in the case where the Company’s Stock Plan is not assumed in an acquisition.  The Company has never adjusted or amended the exercise price of any stock options previously awarded, whether through amendment, cancellation, replacement grant, repricing, or any other means.  Except as set forth in the Restated Certificate, the Company has no obligation (contingent or otherwise) to purchase or redeem any of its capital stock.
409A.  The Company believes in good faith that any “nonqualified deferred compensation plan” (as such term is defined under Section 409A(d)(1) of the Code and the guidance thereunder) under which the Company makes, is obligated to make or promises to make, payments (each, a “409A Plan”) complies in all material respects, in both form and operation, with the requirements of Section 409A of the Code and the guidance thereunder.  To the Company’s knowledge, no payment to be made under any 409A Plan is, or will be, subject to the penalties of Section 409A(a)(1) of the Code.
The Company has obtained valid waivers of any rights by other parties to purchase any of the Shares covered by this Agreement.
Subsidiaries.  The Company does not currently own or control, directly or indirectly, any interest in any other corporation, partnership, trust, joint venture, limited liability company, association, or other business entity.  The Company is not a participant in any joint venture, partnership or similar arrangement.
Authorization.  All corporate action required to be taken by the Company’s Board of Directors and stockholders in order to authorize the Company to enter into the Transaction Agreements, and to issue the Shares at the Closing and the Common Stock issuable upon conversion of the Shares, has been taken.  All action on the part of the officers of the Company necessary for the execution and delivery of the Transaction Agreements, the performance of all obligations of the Company under the Transaction Agreements to be performed as of the Closing, and the issuance and delivery of the Shares has been taken.  The Transaction Agreements, when executed and delivered by the Company, shall constitute valid and legally binding obligations of the Company, enforceable against the Company in accordance with their respective terms except (i) as limited by applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, fraudulent conveyance, or other laws of general application relating to or affecting the enforcement of creditors’ rights generally, (ii) as limited by laws relating to the availability of specific performance, injunctive relief, or other equitable remedies, or (iii) to the extent the indemnification provisions contained in the Investors’ Rights Agreement and the Indemnification Agreement may be limited by applicable federal or state securities laws.
Valid Issuance of Shares.  The Shares, when issued, sold and delivered in accordance with the terms and for the consideration set forth in this Agreement, will be validly issued, fully paid and nonassessable and free of restrictions on transfer other than restrictions on transfer under the Transaction Agreements, applicable state and federal securities laws and liens or encumbrances created by or imposed by a Purchaser.  Assuming the accuracy of the representations of the Purchasers in Section 3 of this Agreement and subject to the filings described in the Voting Agreement, the Shares will be issued in compliance with all applicable federal and state securities laws.  The Common Stock issuable upon conversion of the Shares has been duly reserved for issuance, and upon issuance in accordance with the terms of the Restated Certificate, will be validly issued, fully paid and nonassessable and free of restrictions on transfer other than restrictions on transfer under the Transaction Agreements, applicable federal and state securities laws and liens or encumbrances created by or imposed by a Purchaser.  Assuming the accuracy of the representations of the Purchasers in Section 3 of this Agreement and in the Voting Agreement, the Common Stock issuable upon conversion of the Shares will be issued in compliance with all applicable federal and state securities laws.
Governmental Consents and Filings.  Assuming the accuracy of the representations made by the Purchasers in Section 3 of this Agreement, no consent, approval, order or authorization of, or registration, qualification, designation, declaration or filing with, any federal, state or local governmental authority is required on the part of the Company in connection with the consummation of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, except for filings pursuant to applicable securities laws, which have been made or will be made in a timely manner.
Litigation.  There is no claim, action, suit, proceeding, arbitration, complaint, charge or investigation pending or, to the Company’s knowledge, currently threatened (i) against the Company or any officer, director or Key Employee of the Company; (ii) that questions the validity of the Transaction Agreements or the right of the Company to enter into them, or to consummate the transactions contemplated by the Transaction Agreements; or (iii) to the Company’s knowledge, that would reasonably be expected to have, either individually or in the aggregate, a Material Adverse Effect.  Neither the Company nor, to the Company’s knowledge, any of its officers, directors or Key Employees is a party or is named as subject to the provisions of any order, writ, injunction, judgment or decree of any court or government agency or instrumentality (in the case of officers, directors or Key Employees, such as would affect the Company).  There is no action, suit, proceeding or investigation by the Company pending or which the Company intends to initiate.  The foregoing includes, without limitation, actions, suits, proceedings or investigations pending or threatened in writing (or any basis therefor known to the Company) involving the prior employment of any of the Company’s employees, their services provided in connection with the Company’s business, any information or techniques allegedly proprietary to any of their former employers or their obligations under any agreements with prior employers.
Intellectual Property.
The Company owns or possesses or can acquire on commercially reasonable terms sufficient legal rights to all Company Intellectual Property without any conflict with, or infringement of, the rights of others, including prior employees or consultants; provided that as to patents and trademarks, such representation is made to the Company’s knowledge only.  The Company has not received any communications alleging that the Company has violated, or by conducting its business, would violate any Intellectual Property of any other Person.
No product or service marketed or sold (or proposed to be marketed or sold) by the Company violates or will violate any license or infringes or will infringe any Intellectual Property rights of any other Person; provided that as to patents and trademarks, such representation is made to the Company’s knowledge only.
Other than with respect to (i) commercially available third-party software-based products under standard end-user license and services agreements, (ii) Open Source Software licenses, and (iii) Confidential Information Agreements, There are no outstanding options, licenses, agreements, claims, encumbrances or shared ownership interests of any kind relating to the Company Intellectual Property, nor is the Company bound by or a party to any options, licenses or agreements of any kind with respect to the Intellectual Property of any other Person.
The Company has obtained and possesses valid licenses to use all of the software programs present on the computers and other software-enabled electronic devices that it owns or leases or that it has otherwise provided to its employees for their use in connection with the Company’s business.
Each employee and consultant has assigned to the Company all Intellectual Property that such employee or consultant solely or jointly conceived, reduced to practice, developed or made during the period of their employment or consulting relationship with the Company that (i) relate, at the time of conception, reduction to practice, development, or making of such Intellectual Property, to the Company’s business as then conducted or as then proposed to be conducted, (ii) were developed on any amount of the Company’s time or with the use of any of the Company’s equipment, supplies, facilities or information or (iii) resulted from the performance of services for the Company.  It will not be necessary to use any inventions or other Intellectual Property of any of its employees or consultants (or Persons it currently intends to hire) made prior to their employment by the Company, including prior employees or consultants.
Section 2.8(f) of the Disclosure Schedule lists all patents, patent applications, trademarks, trademark applications, service marks, service mark applications, tradenames, copyrights and domain names, and licenses to and under any of the foregoing, in each case owned or purported to be owned by the Company.
The Company has not embedded, used or distributed any open source, copyleft or community source code (including but not limited to any libraries or code, software, technologies or other materials that are licensed or distributed under any General Public License, Lesser General Public License or similar license arrangement or other distribution model described by the Open Source Initiative at www.opensource.org, collectively “Open Source Software”) in connection with any of its products or services that are generally available or in development in any manner that would materially restrict the ability of the Company to protect its proprietary interests in any such product or service or in any manner that requires, or purports to require (i) any Company Intellectual Property owned by the Company be disclosed or distributed in source code form or be licensed for the purpose of making derivative works; (ii) any restriction on the consideration to be charged for the distribution of any Company Intellectual Property owned by the Company; (iii) the creation of any obligation for the Company with respect to Company Intellectual Property owned by the Company, or the grant to any third party of any rights or immunities under Company Intellectual Property owned by the Company; or (iv) any other limitation, restriction or condition on the right of the Company with respect to its use or distribution of any Company Intellectual Property owned by the Company.  Schedule 2.8(g) of the Disclosure Schedule contains a complete and accurate list of all Open Source Software utilized by the Company.
No government funding, facilities of a university, college, other educational institution or research center, or funding from third parties was used in the development of any Company Intellectual Property owned or purported to be owned by the Company.  No Person who was involved in, or who contributed to, the creation or development of any Company Intellectual Property owned or purported to be owned by the Company, has performed services for the government, university, college, or other educational institution or research center in a manner that would affect Company’s rights in such Company Intellectual Property.
Compliance with Other Instruments.  The Company is not in violation or default (i) of any provisions of its Restated Certificate or Bylaws, (ii) of any instrument, judgment, order, writ or decree, (iii) under any note, indenture or mortgage, or (iv) under any lease, agreement, contract or purchase order to which it is a party or by which it is bound that is required to be listed on the Disclosure Schedule, or (v) of any provision of federal or state statute, rule or regulation applicable to the Company, the violation of which would have a Material Adverse Effect. Except for the Transaction Agreements, There are no agreements, understandings, instruments, contracts or proposed transactions to which the Company is a party or by which it is bound that involve (i) obligations (contingent or otherwise) of, or payments to, the Company in excess of $25,000, (ii) the license of any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret or other proprietary right to or from the Company, (iii) the grant of rights to manufacture, produce, assemble, license, market, or sell its products to any other Person that limit the Company’s exclusive right to develop, manufacture, assemble, distribute, market or sell its products, or (iv) indemnification by the Company with respect to infringements of proprietary rights.

*1) A $2M pre priced round is a down round vs Seed, and it triggers anti-dilution.*
Series Seed was sold at *$0.9830/share*.
Your Restated Certificate has *broad-based weighted average anti-dilution*: if you issue stock (or “deemed issued” via convertibles) below the current Conversion Price, the Series Seed Conversion Price ratchets down using *CP2 = CP1 * (A + B) ÷ (A + C)*.
Practical effect: a $2M pre priced round will *increase the as-converted share count of Seed*, which *dilutes founders/common more than the headline pre-money suggests*.
*2) You cannot just “issue new shares / a new series” without Preferred consent.*
The Restated Certificate requires Preferred approval (voting as a class on an as-converted basis) for major actions, including:
changing Seed rights
increasing/decreasing authorized Preferred or any additional class/series
• creating a new class/series *unless it is junior* to Preferred
• M&A / liquidation
• dividends/redemptions, subsidiary structure, and even changing board size
*3) Griffin already has an explicit right to buy into the “next Preferred round” up to 33% FD.*
Separate Pro Rata Rights Letter: in the *next bona fide sale of a newly authorized series of Preferred*, Griffin can buy enough to end at *33% fully diluted post-close*, at the same price and terms as other investors.
So “we’ll match angels with $250k” is either:
• a voluntary cap [PERSON_NAME_2000] is imposing on itself for this round, or
• a statement that assumes angels are small enough that $250k gets them where they want, or
• something that needs a side letter clarifying how it interacts with their 33% right.
How to structure “[PERSON_NAME_2000] matches angels with $250k at $2M pre” cleanly
Option A (cleanest): One priced round, one price, one security
• *Single financing* at *$2M pre* with *one set of terms* for angels and [PERSON_NAME_2000].
• [PERSON_NAME_2000] subscribes for *up to $250k* on the same terms.
• Add a *short side letter*: [PERSON_NAME_2000]’s $250k cap is intentional, and [PERSON_NAME_2000] either:
*waives* its ability to buy above $250k for this financing (even if the Pro Rata Letter would allow it), or
keeps the right to go above $250k only if needed to reach a specific agreed ownership threshold (spell it out).
Why this matters: if you do two prices or two different securities, you worsen anti-dilution math and increase “unfairness” perceptions immediately.
Option B: Same priced round, two closings
• Close angels first, then close [PERSON_NAME_2000] shortly after, but *same terms, same price, same security*, documented as one “Financing.”
This still preserves [PERSON_NAME_2000]’s Pro Rata framing and keeps the cap table coherent.
Option C (works if [PERSON_NAME_2000] insists on “better than angels” economics): Same security, structured economics (not two valuations)
If [PERSON_NAME_2000] truly wants “lower valuation than angels,” the least messy way is not two prices. Do one price, and give [PERSON_NAME_2000] a negotiated economic lever that is transparent:
• e.g., same Series seed-extension preferred, but [PERSON_NAME_2000] gets a narrow, defined sweetener (board observer, information covenant, small warrant coverage, etc.).
This still likely needs Preferred consents, but it avoids triggering extra anti-dilution complexity from two separate effective prices.
What to avoid: SAFE at a much lower cap as a workaround. Your charter’s adjustment provisions explicitly contemplate Options/Convertible Securities and can defer adjustments until the economics are calculable, but it does not mean “no anti-dilution impact.”

Your direct question: “How do co-founders maintain their shares without investing cash?”
They can’t maintain *percentage ownership* in an equity financing without someone else taking the dilution. There are only three real levers:
1. *Accept dilution* (they keep their absolute share count, but ownership percent drops).

I will break down why and how to Push it to the low end.
I am not your lawyer or accountant, so treat this as planning guidance and sanity check, not formal advice.

1. What drives the cost
Key factors that matter for Harmony Games specifically:
1. *Type of company and complexity*
    ◦ Delaware C-corp with investors and a real cap table.
    ◦ Multiple SAFEs / equity holders.
    ◦ Employment / contractor agreements across countries.
    ◦ Multiple commercial contracts (publishers, ad networks, platforms, vendors).
2. More complexity pushes you away from “simple startup dissolution” pricing and into custom work.
3. *Where fees show up*
4.  You are not just paying for “file a dissolution form”:
    ◦ corporate / securities law work.
    ◦ Contract review and termination.
    ◦ Employment and IP issues.
    ◦ Tax and accounting cleanup.
    ◦ Possibly some board / investor process work (consents, releases, etc.).
5. *Your goal*
    ◦ If you want a “clean, defendable shutdown” that future investors and acquirers will not side-eye, you will spend more than the absolute bare minimum.
    ◦ If you are ok with more “duct tape,” you can cut costs, but you increase risk of something biting you later.
2. Rough fee ranges by category
These are order-of-magnitude numbers for a company like yours, using a mix of decent startup counsel + a scrappy accountant, not BigLaw overkill.
A. corporate dissolution & governance: *10k–30k*
Covers things like:
• Board and stockholder approvals.
• Formal dissolution with Delaware, plus any foreign registrations (e.g. NC, CA, WA).
• Handling investor rights, preference stack, and confirming There is no distribution or a small pro-rata distribution.
• Drafting or reviewing:
    ◦ Plan of liquidation / dissolution.
    ◦ Officer certificates.
    ◦ Releases and indemnities where needed.
If everything is organized and you work with current counsel efficiently, you might land around *10k–15k*. If lots of custom questions, messy history, or negotiations, *20k–30k*.
B. Contracts, IP, and “shutting the business off”: *5k–20k*
Includes:
• Reviewing and terminating:
    ◦ publishing deals (Boombit, CrazyGames, etc.).
    ◦ Platform agreements ([ORG_NAME_0308], IronSource, ad networks).
    ◦ Vendor and contractor agreements.
• Cleaning up IP:
    ◦ Making sure all game code and assets are properly assigned to the company, so There is no surprise claim later.
    ◦ Deciding what happens to IP: kept in the entity that will be dissolved, sold, or assigned to founders or a new entity.
• Dealing with licenses (engine, SDKs) and privacy / data issues.
If you have reasonably standard contracts and you are willing to send most termination notices yourself, lawyer time can be *5k–10k*. If There is negotiation, disputes, or an IP transfer / sale, *15k–20k+* is possible.
C. Employment, severance, and international wrinkles: *5k–20k*
You have:
• At least one US employee (WA).
• Contractors or employees in Turkey / Balkans / El Salvador, etc.
Items:
• Drafting or reviewing separation/severance agreements.
• Making sure state and country-specific rules are respected (notice, unused PTO, local labor rules).
• Confirming There are no outstanding claims or obvious liabilities.
If headcount is small and fairly aligned and you keep severance simple, legal review might be *5k–10k*. If you need local counsel in multiple countries or any disputes, *15k–20k+*.
D. Tax, accounting, and filings (non-legal): *5k–15k*
This is not legal fees but you have to budget it together:
• Final federal and state Tax returns.
• Sales tax / VAT cleanups if relevant.
• Final payroll / 1099s / T4s / foreign equivalents.
• Closing books, documenting treatment of remaining assets and liabilities.
A lean setup with a good startup CPA who already knows your books might be *5k–8k*. If There is multi-state, multi-country complexity and messy historical books, *10k–15k+*.
E. Contingency and “stuff you didn’t think of”: *5k–10k*
Even with good planning you will get:
• Extra questions from investors.
• A weird contract clause someone finds late.
• A platform or partner who needs a custom letter.
Having *5k–10k* in reserve avoids getting stuck mid-process.

3. Putting it together
For a harmonygames-like profile (Delaware C-corp, external investors, small global team, several commercial agreements, no massive litigation):
• *Very lean scenario, disciplined, everything clean:*
    ◦ Legal: 15k–25k
    ◦ accounting / tax: 5k–8k
    ◦ Contingency: 5k
    ◦ *Total: ~25k–38k*
• *More realistic “not perfect but not a mess” scenario:*
    ◦ Legal: 25k–45k
    ◦ accounting / tax: 8k–12k
    ◦ Contingency: 5k–10k
    ◦ *Total: ~38k–67k*
• *If things are messy or negotiated (IP sale, disputes, local counsel in multiple countries):*
    ◦ Legal: 40k–70k
    ◦ accounting / tax: 10k–15k
    ◦ Contingency: 10k
    ◦ *Total: ~60k–95k*
If you want a single planning number, I would assume *50k all-in* as a defensible budget, then work aggressively to drive it down.

4. How to Push toward the low end
If you decide to seriously plan for this, concrete things you can do now so fees do not explode:
1. *Organize everything:*
    ◦ Clean cap table and stock / SAFE docs in one folder.
• All major contracts in one spreadsheet with:
        ▪︎ Counterparty
        ▪︎ Term / termination clause
    ◦ Notice period
    ◦ Employment / contractor agreements and any option grants clearly filed.
2. *Standardize the exit pattern:*
• Decide in advance:
        ▪︎ Severance formula, if any.
        ▪︎ End dates and communication plan.
    ◦ What happens to IP.
    ◦ Then ask counsel to just “paper this plan,” not design it from scratch.
3. *Have existing counsel give a scoped quote:*
• Ask for:
        ▪︎ A fixed or capped fee for core dissolution package.
    ◦ Hourly for “extras” like complex negotiations or IP sale.
    ◦ Get at least one alternative quote from a smaller startup firm.
4. *Do founder work where possible:*
    ◦ Draft first pass of partner termination emails.
    ◦ Fill out standard forms where allowed.
    ◦ Only loop counsel for review and the parts that carry legal risk.
5. What I would actually do in your shoes
If you are purely planning, not pulling the plug:
• Mentally earmark *50k* as “shutdown runway” in your long-range model.
• In the next quiet window, email current counsel something like:
    ◦ “If we needed to do an orderly dissolution with no contentious issues and minimal distributions, roughly what ballpark would you expect in fees, and what can we do now to make that lower?”
• Make sure your books and cap table are clean enough that you can actually execute a shutdown without a 3-month archaeology project.

That is enough to pull you back into \\u201cneed to think\\u201d without nuking average players.\\n4) Optional, still simple: a 3-bucket \\u201cskill\\u201d correction\\nThis keeps the fully-upgraded-but-crappy player from getting obliterated instantly, while still letting them struggle.\\nDefine `S` from the last 3 to 5 levels using only cheap telemetry:\\n\\u2022 attempts per level\\n\\u2022 time to clear\\n\\u2022 waves reached at death (if you have it)\\n\\u2022 number of refreshes (if relevant)\\nBucket it:\\n\\u2022 *Strong*: low attempts, fast clears\\n\\u2022 *Average*: middle\\n\\u2022 *Weak*: high attempts, slow clears\\nThen:\\n\\u2022 `M_skill = {Strong: 1.05, Average: 1.00, Weak: 0.95}`\\nFinal:\\n\\u2022 `M = M_upg * M_skill` (still clamped to 0.85 to 1.25)\\n5) Apply M to a small set of knobs only\\nDo not touch everything. Pick 2 to 3 levers that reliably create \\u201cI have to rebuild now\\u201d moments.\\nGood candidates:\\n\\u2022 enemy HP (or base health pool per wave)\\n\\u2022 enemy damage (or time-to-death pressure)\\n\\u2022 obstacle density or obstacle removal cost\\n\\u2022 shape pool entropy (only if it is a main difficulty driver, and you can change it safely)\\nExample:\\n\\u2022 `EnemyHP = BaseEnemyHP(level, wave) * M`\\n\\u2022 `EnemyDPS = BaseEnemyDPS(level, wave) * (0.5 + 0.5*M)`\\n(less aggressive than HP if DPS spikes feel unfair)\\nA/B test design\\n*Control (A)*: current level-based curve.\\n*Variant (B)*: same curve times `M` (upgrade-adjusted, plus optional skill bucket).\\nPrimary success criteria (pick 2 to avoid overfitting):\\n\\u2022 level completion rate and attempts distribution (especially levels 10 to 25)\\n\\u2022 time per level and \\u201crebuild events\\u201d frequency proxy (big board changes, silver spend spikes, obstacle removals)\\n\\u2022 D1 and D3 retention (segmented by payer vs non-payer, and by upgrade delta buckets)\\nKey segmentation to validate the exact argument in your thread:\\n\\u2022 `delta >= +2` (ahead of curve, your \\u201cspender/optimizer\\u201d proxy)\\n\\u2022 `delta between -1 and +1` (on-curve average)\\n\\u2022 `delta <= -2` (behind curve)\\nExpected outcome if this works:\\n\\u2022 ahead-of-curve players stop cruising for 10 levels, they hit meaningful rebuilds earlier (around level 11 to 12 if that\\u2019s your target)\\n\\u2022 average players stay near current difficulty\\n\\u2022 weak players still struggle, but not catastrophically earlier than today (your existing retry-based adjustments can remain as the safety net)\\nIf you want the minimum possible engineering change: implement only `M_upg` with a clamped multiplier, apply it to enemy HP only, ship the A/B. That alone will tell you if upgrade variance is the real driver.\", \"channel\": \"C09UHHN6PFZ\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\", \"thread_ts\": \"1769885600.421359\"}, {\"ts\": \"1769883061.376529\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Impact of win rate on progression (completion proxy)\\nv1.0.26: win rate strongly predicts progression\\nUsing levels with at least *30 users* at both level L and L+1:\\n*Pearson correlation* between *win rate* and *progression rate*: *r = 0.64*, *p = 0.00016*\\n\\u2022 Simple linear fit: *+10 percentage points win rate* is associated with about *+2.1 percentage points* higher progression to the next level.\\nBucket view (v1.0.26)\\nAverage progression by win-rate band:\\n\\u2022 *Win < 0.40*: progression \\u2248 *0.84*\\n\\u2022 *Win 0.60 to 0.80*: progression \\u2248 *0.92*\\n\\u2022 *Win \\u2265 0.80*: progression \\u2248 *0.965*\\nSo moving a level from \\u201cpain\\u201d (<40% win) to \\u201chealthy\\u201d (\\u226580% win) is roughly *+12 to +13 points* in next-level progression on average.\\nWhy this matters: it compounds fast\\nEven small per-level progression changes multiply across levels. This directly addresses \\u201cahead early, stays ahead for 10+ levels.\\u201d\\n1) Compute an upgrade power score\\nUse what you already have (HP, Regen, Attack upgrades). Start linear.\\n\\u2022 `U = 0.4 * HP + 0.3 * Regen + 0.3 * Attack`\\n(Adjust weights later if Attack dominates outcomes, but start here.)\\n2) Maintain an expected upgrade curve by level\\nYou need `E[level] = expected U at this level` from either:\\ndesign intent (a table), or\\n\\u2022 median `U` from live data per level (better once you have enough data).\\n3) Convert \\u201cahead/behind\\u201d into a difficulty multiplier\\n\\u2022 `delta = U - E[level]`\\n\\u2022 `M_upg = clamp(1 + k * delta, 0.85, 1.25)`\\nWhere `k` is small (start `k = 0.05`).\\nExample using your comment \\u201c3 to 4 levels ahead\\u201d: if that maps to `delta = +2`, then `M_upg = 1.10`. That is enough to pull you back into \\u201cneed to think\\u201d without nuking average players.\\n4) Optional, still simple: a 3-bucket \\u201cskill\\u201d correction\\nThis keeps the fully-upgraded-but-crappy player from getting obliterated instantly, while still letting them struggle.\\nDefine `S` from the last 3 to 5 levels using only cheap telemetry:\\n\\u2022 attempts per level\\n\\u2022 time to clear\\n\\u2022 waves reached at death (if you have it)\\n\\u2022 number of refreshes (if relevant)\\nBucket it:\\n\\u2022 *Strong*: low attempts, fast clears\\n\\u2022 *Average*: middle\\n\\u2022 *Weak*: high attempts, slow clears\\nThen:\\n\\u2022 `M_skill = {Strong: 1.05, Average: 1.00, Weak: 0.95}`\\nFinal:\\n\\u2022 `M = M_upg * M_skill` (still clamped to 0.85 to 1.25)\\n5) Apply M to a small set of knobs only\\nDo not touch everything. Pick 2 to 3 levers that reliably create \\u201cI have to rebuild now\\u201d moments.\\nGood candidates:\\n\\u2022 enemy HP (or base health pool per wave)\\n\\u2022 enemy damage (or time-to-death pressure)\\n\\u2022 obstacle density or obstacle removal cost\\n\\u2022 shape pool entropy (only if it is a main difficulty driver, and you can change it safely)\\nExample:\\n\\u2022 `EnemyHP = BaseEnemyHP(level, wave) * M`\\n\\u2022 `EnemyDPS = BaseEnemyDPS(level, wave) * (0.5 + 0.5*M)`\\n(less aggressive than HP if DPS spikes feel unfair)\\nA/B test design\\n*Control (A)*: current level-based curve.\\n*Variant (B)*: same curve times `M` (upgrade-adjusted, plus optional skill bucket).\\nPrimary success criteria (pick 2 to avoid overfitting):\\n\\u2022 level completion rate and attempts distribution (especially levels 10 to 25)\\n\\u2022 time per level and \\u201crebuild events\\u201d frequency proxy (big board changes, silver spend spikes, obstacle removals)\\n\\u2022 D1 and D3 retention (segmented by payer vs non-payer, and by upgrade delta buckets)\\nKey segmentation to validate the exact argument in your thread:\\n\\u2022 `delta >= +2` (ahead of curve, your \\u201cspender/optimizer\\u201d proxy)\\n\\u2022 `delta between -1 and +1` (on-curve average)\\n\\u2022 `delta <= -2` (behind curve)\\nExpected outcome if this works:\\n\\u2022 ahead-of-curve players stop cruising for 10 levels, they hit meaningful rebuilds earlier (around level 11 to 12 if that\\u2019s your target)\\n\\u2022 average players stay near current difficulty\\n\\u2022 weak players still struggle, but not catastrophically earlier than today (your existing retry-based adjustments can remain as the safety net)\\nIf you want the minimum possible engineering change: implement only `M_upg` with a clamped multiplier, apply it to enemy HP only, ship the A/B. That alone will tell you if upgrade variance is the real driver.\", \"channel\": \"C09UHHN6PFZ\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\", \"thread_ts\": \"1769885600.421359\"}, {\"ts\": \"1769883061.376529\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Impact of win rate on progression (completion proxy)\\nv1.0.26: win rate strongly predicts progression\\nUsing levels with at least *30 users* at both level L and L+1:\\n*Pearson correlation* between *win rate* and *progression rate*: *r = 0.64*, *p = 0.00016*\\n\\u2022 Simple linear fit: *+10 percentage points win rate* is associated with about *+2.1 percentage points* higher progression to the next level.\\nBucket view (v1.0.26)\\nAverage progression by win-rate band:\\n\\u2022 *Win < 0.40*: progression \\u2248 *0.84*\\n\\u2022 *Win 0.60 to 0.80*: progression \\u2248 *0.92*\\n\\u2022 *Win \\u2265 0.80*: progression \\u2248 *0.965*\\nSo moving a level from \\u201cpain\\u201d (<40% win) to \\u201chealthy\\u201d (\\u226580% win) is roughly *+12 to +13 points* in next-level progression on average.\\nWhy this matters: it compounds fast\\nEven small per-level progression changes multiply across levels. Example starting with 1,000 players:\\n10 levels at 0.85 progression: ~*197* players remain\\n\\u2022 10 levels at 0.93 progression: ~*484* players remain\\nSpecific pain points to look at (v1.0.26)\\nLevels that combine low win rate and/or unusually low progression:\\n\\u2022 *Level 3*: win *0.49*, progression *0.73* (big drop)\\n\\u2022 *Level 4*: win *0.25*, progression *0.816*\\n\\u2022 *Level 6*: win *0.37*, progression *0.826*\\n\\u2022 *Level 7*: win *0.29*, progression *0.873*\\nAlso: *Level 2* has win *0.79* but progression *0.78*, that suggests an onboarding or intent filter issue (players leaving for reasons other than \\u201cI can\\u2019t beat it\\u201d).\\n\\nVersion-to-version comparison (what you can and can\\u2019t conclude)\\nYou can compare versions reliably only where both have adequate N. With the 30+ user filter, that\\u2019s basically *levels 1 to 5*.\\nIn those levels:\\n\\u2022 v1.0.72 win rate is higher than v1.0.26 (sometimes much higher),\\n\\u2022 but progression is not consistently higher, which points to cohort differences, tracking differences, or other funnel effects beyond pure difficulty.\\nWhat to do next (to answer \\u201ccompletion rate\\u201d cleanly)\\nIf you want true \\u201ccompletion rate\\u201d and not a proxy, you need per level, per version:\\n\\u2022 *unique starters*\\n*unique completers*\\n\\u2022 optionally *attempts per user*, *time-to-win*, *churn after loss*\\nThen compute:\\n\\u2022 *Completion rate* = completers / starters\\n\\u2022 *Progression* = starters(L+1) / starters(L)\\n\\u2022 And run a per-level model: completion or progression as a function of win rate, controlling for level and cohort.\\nIf you upload the underlying starts/completes table (or a per-user attempt table), I\\u2019ll produce the proper completion-rate plots and quantify the causal-looking relationship more tightly.\", \"channel\": \"C09UHHN6PFZ\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\", \"thread_ts\": \"1769883057.049209\"}, {\"ts\": \"1769879315.783389\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"or if you want to use the same container we can add a third option of 140 gems so it would be 3 containers\\n\\u2022 Buy 1 chest for 30 \\n\\u2022 buy 5 chest for 140\\n\\u2022 buy 10 chest for 270\", \"channel\": \"C09UHHN6PFZ\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1769877425.422219\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Final chest implementation is very confusing to me. • Given our current runway of less than a month and obligations, continuing would create risk without a responsible probability of success.

What the R&D credit is based on
The federal R&D credit is calculated *for the tax year*, not by quarter, using *Qualified Research Expenses (QREs)*, which commonly include:
• *W-2 wages* for employees doing qualified R&D work
• *Supplies* used in qualified research
• *Contract research* (generally *65%* of eligible amounts) 
So “Q4 payroll was zero” only reduces the credit if it means your *annual* qualified wages were low. If you had meaningful qualified payroll in Q1 to Q3, it still counts for the year.
Why you may “get nothing” even if you have a credit
The credit generally reduces *tax you owe*. If you owe *no federal income tax*, the credit may not produce a refund, it usually becomes a carryforward. The IRS describes the credit as computed on Form 6765.
For many businesses, unused general business credits can be carried forward (commonly up to *20 years*).
The startup payroll tax offset (only matters if you have payroll tax)
If you qualified and made the election, you can apply some of the R&D credit against *employer payroll taxes*, but it is limited to the employer share of *social Security* (and, since 2023, potentially *Medicare* for any remaining amount).
Key implication for your question:
If your *Q4 payroll taxes were near zero*, you likely could not use much credit *in that quarter*.
Unused payroll-offset credit can *carry forward to later quarters*, but only helps if you have future payroll tax liability.
• You must elect it properly on *Form 6765*, and then apply it on payroll filings using *Form 8974*. 
Practical answer for “we spent $4K, did we get nothing?”
You “get nothing” in the real-world sense if all of the below are true:
1. *Very low annual QREs* (for you this is often wages, but could include contractor R&D)
2. *No federal income tax due* for the year
3. *No meaningful payroll tax going forward* (especially if shutting down), so you cannot use the payroll offset carryforward either
If (2) and (3) are true, you may still technically have a credit on paper, but it may never turn into cash savings.
What to check quickly (no theory, just signals)
Your *total 2025 qualified wages* for R&D (not just Q4).
Whether your $4K provider included *contractor R&D* or only W-2 wages (contract research can count at 65%).
• Whether you had *any income tax liability* to offset, or whether you elected the *payroll tax offset* and have (or will have) payroll tax to absorb it.

• 2,746,693 / 10,172,939 = *~27.0%*
2) What [PERSON_NAME_2000] must invest to stay undiluted in a $500K round
Rule: *Required check = current % ownership × total new money*
• *0.27 × $500,000 = ~$135,000*
So:
If [PERSON_NAME_2000] invests *~$135K*, they stay roughly flat.
• If [PERSON_NAME_2000] invests *$250K*, they are *over-pro-rata*, they *increase* ownership (they are not diluted).
This is true regardless of whether the pre-money is $10M, $2M, or anything else. Valuation changes _how much_ they increase, not whether they can be kept flat.

Bottom line
*There is no “required valuation”* to keep [PERSON_NAME_2000] undiluted.

*1) A $2M pre priced round is a down round vs Seed, and it triggers anti-dilution.*
Series Seed was sold at *$0.9830/share*.
Your Restated Certificate has *broad-based weighted average anti-dilution*: if you issue stock (or “deemed issued” via convertibles) below the current Conversion Price, the Series Seed Conversion Price ratchets down using *CP2 = CP1 * (A + B) ÷ (A + C)*.
Practical effect: a $2M pre priced round will *increase the as-converted share count of Seed*, which *dilutes founders/common more than the headline pre-money suggests*.
*2) You cannot just “issue new shares / a new series” without Preferred consent.*
The Restated Certificate requires Preferred approval (voting as a class on an as-converted basis) for major actions, including:
changing Seed rights
increasing/decreasing authorized Preferred or any additional class/series
• creating a new class/series *unless it is junior* to Preferred
• M&A / liquidation
• dividends/redemptions, subsidiary structure, and even changing board size
*3) Griffin already has an explicit right to buy into the “next Preferred round” up to 33% FD.*
Separate Pro Rata Rights Letter: in the *next bona fide sale of a newly authorized series of Preferred*, Griffin can buy enough to end at *33% fully diluted post-close*, at the same price and terms as other investors.
So “we’ll match angels with $250k” is either:
• a voluntary cap [PERSON_NAME_2000] is imposing on itself for this round, or
• a statement that assumes angels are small enough that $250k gets them where they want, or
• something that needs a side letter clarifying how it interacts with their 33% right.
How to structure “[PERSON_NAME_2000] matches angels with $250k at $2M pre” cleanly
Option A (cleanest): One priced round, one price, one security
• *Single financing* at *$2M pre* with *one set of terms* for angels and [PERSON_NAME_2000].
• [PERSON_NAME_2000] subscribes for *up to $250k* on the same terms.
• Add a *short side letter*: [PERSON_NAME_2000]’s $250k cap is intentional, and [PERSON_NAME_2000] either:
*waives* its ability to buy above $250k for this financing (even if the Pro Rata Letter would allow it), or
keeps the right to go above $250k only if needed to reach a specific agreed ownership threshold (spell it out).
Why this matters: if you do two prices or two different securities, you worsen anti-dilution math and increase “unfairness” perceptions immediately.
Option B: Same priced round, two closings
• Close angels first, then close [PERSON_NAME_2000] shortly after, but *same terms, same price, same security*, documented as one “Financing.”
This still preserves [PERSON_NAME_2000]’s Pro Rata framing and keeps the cap table coherent.
Option C (works if [PERSON_NAME_2000] insists on “better than angels” economics): Same security, structured economics (not two valuations)
If [PERSON_NAME_2000] truly wants “lower valuation than angels,” the least messy way is not two prices. Do one price, and give [PERSON_NAME_2000] a negotiated economic lever that is transparent:
• e.g., same Series seed-extension preferred, but [PERSON_NAME_2000] gets a narrow, defined sweetener (board observer, information covenant, small warrant coverage, etc.).
This still likely needs Preferred consents, but it avoids triggering extra anti-dilution complexity from two separate effective prices.
What to avoid: SAFE at a much lower cap as a workaround. Your charter’s adjustment provisions explicitly contemplate Options/Convertible Securities and can defer adjustments until the economics are calculable, but it does not mean “no anti-dilution impact.”

Your direct question: “How do co-founders maintain their shares without investing cash?”
They can’t maintain *percentage ownership* in an equity financing without someone else taking the dilution. There are only three real levers:
1. *Accept dilution* (they keep their absolute share count, but ownership percent drops).
2. *Get a “founder refresh”* (new option grants or restricted stock grants). This dilutes everyone else and typically requires Board approval and, depending on what needs to change (authorized shares, charter/bylaws, new series), may trigger Preferred consent.
3. *Pay-to-play / recap mechanics* that shift dilution onto non-participating investors. This is exactly what pay-to-play is for, but it requires negotiating and documenting changes to Preferred economics and rights, which are protected by the consent items listed in the Restated Certificate.

a small *founder option refresh* sized explicitly (example: 5–10% post-money pool allocated to founders/retention), and
• a *pay-to-play* feature where insiders who do not participate lose some combination of anti-dilution protection, pro rata, or Preferred status (conversion to common), subject to negotiation.

Each has tradeoffs, but all are common.
1) Cofounders invest a token amount, and the rest is “earned” via retention or milestones
• founders put in something credible (even small), then get a board-approved “founder retention” grant or option refresh tied to staying 6 to 12 months and hitting milestones.
• Effect: founders do not need to match investor checks dollar-for-dollar, but they are not getting a free pass either.
2) Put founder common into a reverse-vesting schedule
• founders agree some portion of their existing common is subject to vesting again over 12 to 24 months.
• This reduces investor fear that founders keep full ownership without funding the bridge.
• Effect: founders keep shares if they stay and execute, they forfeit unvested portion if they leave.
3) Management incentive pool (MIP) created as part of the recap
• Company creates a pool (often 10 to 20% post-money in distressed situations) reserved for founders and key operators, issued as options or restricted stock.
• Investors accept dilution because it is explicitly the cost of having the team that can create value.
• Effect: founders can be re-incentivized without writing a check, but it must be negotiated and approved.
4) Convert unpaid founder salary into the financing (salary deferral note)
• founders formally defer cash comp and accrue it as a note that converts in the bridge at the same terms (or slightly worse) as investors.
• Effect: founders are “investing” via forgone salary, which investors often view as real skin in the game.
5) Founder loan to the company, even if small
• founders put in any amount they can (often 10k to 50k), documented as a convertible note in the same round.
• Effect: simple, clean signal, helps with optics. Not always feasible.
6) Carve-out protection in the term sheet (limited founder dilution)
• Term sheet explicitly says: founders will not be diluted below X% fully diluted if they remain employed and hit milestones.
• This is essentially a negotiated founder carve-out.
• Effect: very direct, but investors may Push back unless the company is truly founder-led value creation.

content.content: {"result":"{\"ok\": true, \"messages\": [{\"ts\": \"1757542054.939119\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"so the next one is biz summary: Harmony Games is an AI-driven mobile studio building the next breakout in puzzle-RPG. Our mission is simple: take many high-quality shots on goal, move fast, and scale only when the data says we\\u2019ve earned it.\\n\\nAt the center is Harmony Games Engine\\u2014our reusable production platform that puts AI in the loop for level creation, adaptive difficulty, event scheduling (the \\u201clive service\\u201d layer), economy tuning, analytics, and creative testing. v1 took ~15 months to build; now we can port the stack into a new title in ~4 months with production quality. The result is fewer one-off builds, faster iteration, and a small team that learns cheaper than traditional studios.\\n\\nOur first franchise with a break-through potential is Zombie Match 3D, introducing a new \\u201cMatch & Slash\\u201d subgenre: fast 3D matching where every match becomes a weapon, layered with items, upgrades, bosses, and horde modes. The game is live in early tests (alpha) with a growing content slate and service layer. Early UK iOS signals on minimal polish: ~34% day-one retention and ~25 minutes first-day playtime with only 100 levels and minimal polish. Over the next 4\\u20136 weeks we\\u2019ll expand to 500+ levels, add more polish/VFX, and scale tests to 2\\u20133k users. Go/No-Go gates are explicit: \\u226545% day-one retention, \\u226545% day-seven-to-day-one retention ratio, and \\u2264$3.50 CPI in UK iOS. We scale only if we clear the gates. If not, we\\u2019ll pivot to our next title\\n\\nOn the platform roadmap, we\\u2019re evolving AI from \\u201cassistant\\u201d to \\u201cjunior designer\\u201d toward a data-driven designer that adapts difficulty, rewards, and pacing from live player data. tool_use_result.content: {"result":"{\"ok\": true, \"messages\": [{\"ts\": \"1757542054.939119\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"so the next one is biz summary: Harmony Games is an AI-driven mobile studio building the next breakout in puzzle-RPG. Founded in 2023, we raised a $3M seed led by GRIFFIN GAMING PARTNERS, a multi-billion dollar gaming-focused fund, alongside world-class advisors such as [PERSON_NAME_0090] and Matthew Collins, and assembled a senior, 17-person distributed team across the U.S., Europe, and South America. Our mission is simple: take many high-quality shots on goal, move fast, and scale only when the data says we\\u2019ve earned it.\\n\\nAt the center is Harmony Games Engine\\u2014our reusable production platform that puts AI in the loop for level creation, adaptive difficulty, event scheduling (the \\u201clive service\\u201d layer), economy tuning, analytics, and creative testing. v1 took ~15 months to build; now we can port the stack into a new title in ~4 months with production quality. The result is fewer one-off builds, faster iteration, and a small team that learns cheaper than traditional studios.\\n\\nOur first franchise with a break-through potential is Zombie Match 3D, introducing a new \\u201cMatch & Slash\\u201d subgenre: fast 3D matching where every match becomes a weapon, layered with items, upgrades, bosses, and horde modes. The game is live in early tests (alpha) with a growing content slate and service layer. Early UK iOS signals on minimal polish: ~34% day-one retention and ~25 minutes first-day playtime with only 100 levels and minimal polish. Over the next 4\\u20136 weeks we\\u2019ll expand to 500+ levels, add more polish/VFX, and scale tests to 2\\u20133k users. Go/No-Go gates are explicit: \\u226545% day-one retention, \\u226545% day-seven-to-day-one retention ratio, and \\u2264$3.50 CPI in UK iOS. We scale only if we clear the gates. If not, we\\u2019ll pivot to our next title\\n\\nOn the platform roadmap, we\\u2019re evolving AI from \\u201cassistant\\u201d to \\u201cjunior designer\\u201d toward a data-driven designer that adapts difficulty, rewards, and pacing from live player data. On the service side, our event/offer system already supports leaderboards, quests, calendars, and season passes, with personalization and rapid experiment tooling next.\\n\\nWe\\u2019re raising a $2.5M seed extension for extending runway ~18+ months while we: (1) complete the next Harmony Games Engine milestones and content pipeline ($1.5M), and (2) fund beta and soft-launch user acquisition that will be only used if metrics justify the marketing spend ($1.0M). Burn is ~$100K/month excluding marketing, and we intend to stay lean until a title proves it can scale.\\n\\nWhy Harmony Games: platform-first leverage, disciplined test-kill-scale operating model, and a distinct product wedge with Match & Slash aimed at broad Western audiences\\u2014positioned to stand out in a crowded market and compound into a franchise.\", \"channel\": \"C096HFA5Z8W\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1757286779.102999\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Harmony Games is an AI-driven studio built around Harmony Games Engine, a reusable production and liveops platform that keeps AI in the loop for level design, content ops, and rapid experimentation. The engine lets a lean team ship faster, test more cheaply, and scale potential hits. We build hit-ready puzzle RPGs for Western mobile players and partner studios, with our first franchise being a Match & Slash puzzle RPG with day-one liveops. We monetize through free-to-play in-app purchases and ads, and selectively pursue revenue-share partnerships with large publishing partners.\\n\\n*Stage:* Engine-first mobile game studio focused on puzzle RPGs; bridge/seed extension. {"ok": true, "messages": [{"ts": "1757542054.939119", "type": "message", "text": "so the next one is biz summary: Harmony Games is an AI-driven mobile studio building the next breakout in puzzle-RPG. Founded in 2023, we raised a $3M seed led by GRIFFIN GAMING PARTNERS, a multi-billion dollar gaming-focused fund, alongside world-class advisors such as [PERSON_NAME_0090] and Matthew Collins, and assembled a senior, 17-person distributed team across the U.S., Europe, and South America. Our mission is simple: take many high-quality shots on goal, move fast, and scale only when the data says we’ve earned it.

At the center is Harmony Games Engine—our reusable production platform that puts AI in the loop for level creation, adaptive difficulty, event scheduling (the “live service” layer), economy tuning, analytics, and creative testing. v1 took ~15 months to build; now we can port the stack into a new title in ~4 months with production quality. The result is fewer one-off builds, faster iteration, and a small team that learns cheaper than traditional studios.

Our first franchise with a break-through potential is Zombie Match 3D, introducing a new “Match & Slash” subgenre: fast 3D matching where every match becomes a weapon, layered with items, upgrades, bosses, and horde modes. The game is live in early tests (alpha) with a growing content slate and service layer. Early UK iOS signals on minimal polish: ~34% day-one retention and ~25 minutes first-day playtime with only 100 levels and minimal polish. Over the next 4–6 weeks we’ll expand to 500+ levels, add more polish/VFX, and scale tests to 2–3k users. Go/No-Go gates are explicit: ≥45% day-one retention, ≥45% day-seven-to-day-one retention ratio, and ≤$3.50 CPI in UK iOS. We scale only if we clear the gates. If not, we’ll pivot to our next title

On the platform roadmap, we’re evolving AI from “assistant” to “junior designer” toward a data-driven designer that adapts difficulty, rewards, and pacing from live player data. On the service side, our event/offer system already supports leaderboards, quests, calendars, and season passes, with personalization and rapid experiment tooling next.

We’re raising a $2.5M seed extension for extending runway ~18+ months while we: (1) complete the next Harmony Games Engine milestones and content pipeline ($1.5M), and (2) fund beta and soft-launch user acquisition that will be only used if metrics justify the marketing spend ($1.0M). input.title: Investor letter - wind-down (Feb 2026)
input.bodyText:
Subject: Harmony Games - winding down the company

Hi everyone,

I'm writing to share a difficult update: we have decided to wind down Harmony Games. I wanted each of you to hear it from me first, and this letter sets out where things stand and what it means for you.

What happened
We reached this decision on February 9, 2026, after a thorough review of the most recent data across our products and the realistic set of options in front of us. Despite multiple iterations, we did not get the metrics to a point that supports a viable business path, and we do not have the funding to continue operating while searching for a new direction.
- We built and tested three games on a limited budget, staying true to our mission of hybrid-casual gameplay with RPG depth: Domino Delights (domino/tripeaks solitaire with RPG elements), Zombie Match 3D (a Match Factory style core loop with RPG combat and progression) and Combo Fighter (Tetris-like block gameplay with RPG elements).
- We took real creative risks and explored partnerships and other paths to scale distribution, including a bridge and recap in January, but none changed the trajectory enough. The latest Combo Fighter retention data confirmed we are not investable in our current form.
- We have been in sustained financial hardship since mid-2025; revenue never reached meaningful levels and we ended January with roughly a month of runway.
- The team has stopped. Our remaining contractors' engagements ended on December 31, 2025 and January 31, 2026, and we told the full team on February 11 and sent everyone written termination letters the same day.

Where things stand
- Holders: as of today Carta shows 20 stockholders and optionholders besides the three founders: Griffin Gaming Partners (two funds), eleven angel investors and eight former team members whose options are still within their exercise window. Several former team members' options have already expired.
- Board: the board now consists of me and Robert. Griffin's board representative stepped down on February 12, and we thank him for his support over the last three years.
- Process: we have engaged Sunset, a specialist wind-down firm, to run an orderly dissolution. Their legal team is preparing the Plan of Dissolution and will handle the Delaware dissolution, our withdrawals from California and North Carolina, creditor communications and final tax and accounting close-out. Formal notices and any stockholder approvals will come to you separately from Sunset's legal team.
- Vendors: we have terminated or are closing out all vendor and service contracts, and we expect to cover the company's remaining obligations, including paying off our bank credit line, without leaving debts on anyone's books.

What it means for you
- Distributions: the company is insolvent. After obligations are settled we do not expect any cash to be available for distribution to stockholders, and the preferred stock's preferences do not change that. If anything is left once the dissolution is complete, it will be distributed according to our charter and you will hear from us.
- Tax papers: Sunset will prepare the company's final returns. Any documents you need for your own taxes (for example, to record the loss on your shares) will be sent to you once the dissolution is filed, and your Carta account stays available in the meantime.
- Options: former team members' options can still be exercised until the last day shown in Carta, but because the shares are expected to have no value, we do not recommend exercising. No action is needed; unexercised options simply lapse on their last day.

What happens to the games and the IP
- We are sunsetting the live games in a controlled way and moving player support off third-party tools.
- On February 12 we signed a data licensing agreement for anonymised game data. It brings in enough cash to cover the cost of an orderly wind-down, and the agreement confirms that the company keeps full ownership of its IP.
- We are still evaluating what to do with the remaining IP and codebase (archive, sale or other disposition) and will keep you informed.

Thank you
I regret having to send this. I am proud of the team we put together and the quality of what we shipped. We ran a frugal operation, made multiple bets and pushed hard, but we did not reach the performance required to build a durable company. Thank you for backing us, for your advice and for your patience. I will send short updates as the major steps are completed and once the final position is clear.

If you would like to talk 1:1, reply here and I will make time.

Thank you,
Leonard Hayes
CEO and Co-founder, Harmony Games Inc.
leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co

input.subject: Harmony Games is closing - your options (last day Feb 21)
input.body:
Hi Vincent,

I wanted you to hear this from me directly: we have decided to close Harmony Games. On February 9, after reviewing the latest data across our games, we concluded we could not reach a viable business and no longer have the funding to keep operating. We have engaged a specialist firm to run an orderly wind-down and dissolution of the company.

Your holding: according to Carta you hold 1,530 vested stock options (grant ES-14, 3,866 granted on May 15, 2024). Because your engagement ended on November 21, 2025, the last day to exercise them is February 21, 2026. After that date they lapse automatically.

Since the company is being dissolved and the shares are expected to have no value, we do not recommend exercising. You don't need to do anything; if you take no action the options simply expire on February 21.

Thank you for everything you contributed to Domino Delights. If you have any questions, just reply to this email.

Best,
Leonard

input.subject: Harmony Games is closing - your options (last day April 30)
input.body:
Hi Oliver,

I wanted you to hear this from me directly: we have decided to close Harmony Games. On February 9, after reviewing the latest data across our games, we concluded we could not reach a viable business and no longer have the funding to keep operating. We have engaged a specialist firm to run an orderly wind-down and dissolution of the company.

Your holding: according to Carta you hold 5,404 vested stock options (grant ES-18, 15,259 granted on October 22, 2024; the unvested part ended with your termination effective January 30, 2026). The last day to exercise them is April 30, 2026. After that date they lapse automatically.

Because the company is being dissolved and the shares are expected to have no value, we do not recommend exercising. You don't need to do anything; if you take no action the options simply expire on April 30.

Thank you for everything you engineered for us. If you have any questions, just reply to this email.

Best,
Leonard
